settings.label: Font
settings.description: Any monospace font. Nerd Fonts also show prompt icons.

settings.label: Size
settings.description: Ctrl+0 returns to this size.

settings.label: Weight
settings.description: How heavy normal text is. A font without that weight shows its nearest one.

settings.label: Bold weight
settings.description: How heavy bold text is.

settings.label: Ligatures
settings.description: Fonts that have them (Cascadia Code, JetBrains Mono, Fira Code) join `=>`, `!=`, `->`, and the like into one shape. Each character keeps its own cell, and the character under the cursor isn't joined.

settings.label: Fallback fonts
settings.description: Zinc tries these fonts in order for characters your font lacks, before Windows picks one. Separate them with commas.
settings.placeholder: Symbols Nerd Font, Noto Sans JP
settings.example: Symbols Nerd Font, Noto Sans JP

settings.label: Line height
settings.description: Adds room between lines, as a percentage (20%) or in pixels (2). A negative value gives less room. Text stays centered.

settings.label: Built-in glyphs
settings.description: Zinc draws box lines, blocks, and Powerline shapes itself, so they join up in any font.

settings.label: Line thickness
settings.description: Makes built-in lines thicker or thinner, in pixels (1, -1) or as a percentage (20%).

settings.label: Color scheme
settings.description: About 650 schemes are included. Add your own to the themes folder next to config.toml.

settings.label: Match 256 colors to the scheme
settings.description: Programs that use the extended 256 colors (vim and htop themes) get shades made from the scheme's 16 colors instead of the standard ones.

settings.label: Shades from background to text in light schemes
settings.description: When off, shades run from dark to light, which is what programs expect.

settings.label: Cursor text
settings.description: Colors the character under a block cursor. If the scheme doesn't set one either, it's the background color.

settings.label: Selection
settings.description: Colors the background of selected text. If the scheme doesn't set one either, selection inverts the colors.

settings.label: Selected text
settings.description: If the scheme doesn't set one either, the text keeps its color, or inverts with the selection when "Selection" has no color either.

settings.label: Pane headers
settings.description: Colors the row behind pane titles and tabs. On cards, the border is a step stronger.

choices.label: Same as the terminal
choices.detail: The row matches the terminal's background, and hidden tabs get a shade so the shown tab still stands out. Cards then have no border.

settings.label: Minimum contrast
settings.description: Text that reads poorly against its background turns black or white. 1 turns it off, 4.5 is the usual accessibility level, and 21 makes all text black or white.

settings.label: Bold in bright colors
settings.description: Bold text in the first eight colors shows their bright versions, as older terminals did.

settings.label: Bold text color
settings.description: Colors bold text that's in the default text color.

settings.label: Faint text
settings.description: How bright dim text is. At 1, dim text is as bright as other text.

settings.label: Find highlight
settings.description: Colors the background of each match of Find.

settings.label: Current match
settings.description: Colors the background of the match Find is on.

settings.label: Cursor shape
settings.description: A program can pick its own shape, as vim's insert mode often does.

settings.label: Blinking cursor
settings.description: A program can turn blinking on or off for itself.

settings.label: Cursor opacity
settings.description: At 1, the cursor is solid. Lower values let the character under a block cursor show in its own color.

settings.label: Cursor at the prompt
settings.description: The cursor takes this shape while the shell waits for a command. A program's own cursor still wins. Needs shell integration.

choices.label: Bar
choices.detail: A bar looks like the cursor in a text box.

settings.label: Light or dark
settings.description: Sets the look of Zinc's windows, menus, and dialogs. The terminal keeps its color scheme. Restart Zinc to apply.

choices.label: Same as Windows
choices.detail: Zinc follows "Choose your mode" in Windows Settings > Personalization > Colors.

settings.label: Accent color
settings.description: Colors selections, focus lines, switches, and buttons. Restart Zinc to apply.

choices.label: Windows' accent
choices.detail: Zinc uses the accent color from Windows Settings > Personalization > Colors.

settings.label: Window background
settings.description: What's behind everything in the window: tabs, sidebar, and terminal.

choices.label: Mica
choices.detail: Mica isn't see-through. It takes a tint from your wallpaper, as Windows apps do.

choices.label: Acrylic (frosted)
choices.detail: The windows behind show, blurred.

choices.label: Clear
choices.detail: The windows behind show as they are.

settings.label: Window tint
settings.description: How much color an acrylic or clear background carries. Lower is more see-through.

settings.label: Window tint color
settings.description: The color an acrylic or clear background is tinted with.

settings.label: Terminal background opacity
settings.description: At 1, the background is solid. Lower values let the window background show behind the text. Colored cells stay solid.

settings.label: Custom shaders
settings.description: Effects drawn over the terminal, such as CRT screens, glow, and cursor trails. They're GLSL files written for Ghostty or Shadertoy, and they run in order.

settings.label: Animation
settings.description: Says when animated shaders move. The others redraw only when the terminal changes.

choices.label: While focused
choices.detail: Shaders in unfocused terminals pause where they are. The text under them still updates.

choices.label: Always
choices.detail: Every terminal with shaders keeps redrawing, focused or not.

choices.label: Never
choices.detail: Animated shaders hold still too, cursor effects included, and redraw only when the terminal changes.

settings.label: Padding left and right
settings.description: Adds space between the window's edge and the text.

settings.label: Padding top and bottom
settings.description: Adds space between the window's edge and the text.

settings.label: Even padding
settings.description: Splits the leftover space between both sides. When off, all of it goes to the right and bottom.

settings.label: Workspaces
settings.description: Shows workspaces as tabs along the top, or as a list in a sidebar. Applies to windows opened from now on.

settings.label: Sidebar
settings.description: Applies only when "Workspaces" is "In a sidebar".

choices.label: Auto-hide
choices.detail: The sidebar slides out when the pointer reaches the window's left edge.

settings.label: Title bar
settings.description: Applies only when "Workspaces" is "In a sidebar".

choices.label: Auto-hide
choices.detail: The title bar slides down when the pointer reaches the window's top edge.

settings.label: Start page for new workspaces
settings.description: Lets you choose a profile, a folder, and a name when you open a workspace. Enter starts the default profile.

settings.label: Colors for new workspaces
settings.description: New workspaces you don't color yourself take their colors from this.

choices.label: By folder
choices.detail: A workspace with a folder gets that folder's color, the same one every time.

choices.label: One after another
choices.detail: Each new workspace takes the next color.

settings.label: New tabs and splits start
settings.description: New tabs in a workspace with its own folder start there. Without "Tabs inside panes", this is for splits only, because a new tab is a new workspace.

choices.label: Where you are
choices.detail: Otherwise, a new tab or split starts in the focused terminal's current folder.

choices.label: In the profile's folder
choices.detail: Otherwise, a new tab or split starts in its profile's folder.

settings.label: Tabs inside panes
settings.description: Each pane can hold several tabs.

settings.label: Show pane tabs as
settings.description: Applies only while "Tabs inside panes" is on.

choices.label: Tabs
choices.detail: A pane's header shows a row of tabs. When the tabs don't fit, they shorten, then show only their icons, then fold into a menu.

choices.label: A menu
choices.detail: A pane's header shows the current tab, then a count ("2 of 5") that opens a menu of every tab. Switch tabs with the menu or with keys.

settings.label: Pane headers
settings.description: The row above a pane shows its tabs, or its title when it has one tab.

choices.label: Automatic
choices.detail: Every pane gets a header once its workspace is split, and so does any pane with two or more tabs.

choices.label: With several tabs
choices.detail: Only panes with two or more tabs get a header.

settings.label: Header buttons
settings.description: Shows split, maximize, and other buttons on the right of a pane's header, with a program's progress beside them.

choices.label: Always
choices.detail: Every pane shows the buttons.

choices.label: Focused pane
choices.detail: The focused pane shows the buttons, and the other panes show them while the pointer is over their header.

choices.label: On hover
choices.detail: A pane shows the buttons only while the pointer is over its header. Touch and pen have no hover. The command palette and a pane's right-click menu have every action.

settings.label: Gap between panes
settings.description: Above 0, panes are rounded cards with space between them. At 0 they meet at a thin divider.

settings.label: Gap at the workspace edges
settings.description: Puts the same gap around the outside, split or not, so splitting never moves a pane's outer edges. Applies only when "Gap between panes" is above 0.

settings.label: Show focus with
settings.description: How the focused pane stands out from the others.

choices.label: Ring
choices.detail: The focused pane gets an accent-colored outline.

choices.label: Tab accent
choices.detail: The focused pane gets an accent-colored line along its top.

choices.label: None
choices.detail: Only the dimming of other panes ("Unfocused panes") marks the focused pane. With "Unfocused panes" at 1, nothing does.

settings.label: Pane animations
settings.description: Panes slide into place when you split, close, maximize, or move them. They don't while "Animation effects" is off in Windows Settings.

settings.label: Resize step
settings.description: How far a resize key moves the divider, as a share of the panes it splits.

settings.label: Unfocused panes
settings.description: How bright unfocused panes stay. At 1, they aren't dimmed.

settings.label: Dimming color
settings.description: Unfocused panes fade toward this color.

settings.label: Divider color
settings.description: Colors the line between split panes when "Gap between panes" is 0.

settings.label: Reopen windows
settings.description: Windows, workspaces, splits, and tabs come back in their folders.

choices.label: Automatic
choices.detail: While the quick terminal's hotkey is set, Zinc stays in the tray so the hotkey keeps working. Otherwise it quits.

choices.label: Stay in the tray
choices.detail: Click the tray icon to open a window again.

settings.label: When you sign in to Windows

choices.label: Start in the tray
choices.detail: No window opens. The quick terminal's hotkey works, and the tray icon opens your windows.

choices.label: Open my windows
choices.detail: Your windows open as you left them, or a new window opens.

settings.label: Open in Zinc from File Explorer
settings.description: Adds "Open in Zinc" to the right-click menu of folders and drives. On Windows 11 it's under "Show more options".

settings.label: Ask before closing
settings.description: Asks when a tab, pane, workspace, or window you close still runs a command or holds two or more tabs. Zinc knows a command is running through shell integration.

settings.label: Ask before quitting with a running command
settings.description: Asks when you quit Zinc, or restart it for an update, while a command still runs.

settings.label: Shell integration
settings.description: Marks prompts and commands in PowerShell, bash, and zsh (WSL too), so you can jump between prompts, copy a command's output, and see which commands failed.

settings.label: Command marks
settings.description: Shows a bar beside the output of these commands.

choices.label: Close if it succeeded
choices.detail: When the program fails, the pane stays open so you can read why. Any key then closes the pane.

choices.label: Keep it open
choices.detail: Any key closes the pane.

settings.label: Pick up environment changes
settings.description: New tabs read PATH and other variables from Windows as they start, so an installer's changes work without restarting Zinc.

settings.label: Program titles
settings.description: Shells and programs set the tab's title (often the folder or the running command). When off, tabs show the profile's name.

settings.label: Folder and command as the title
settings.description: Shows the folder at the prompt, and the running command otherwise. A program's own title still wins. Needs shell integration.

settings.label: Scrollback lines
settings.description: How far back you can scroll.

settings.label: Word boundaries
settings.description: These characters end a word when you double-click. Space and tab always do. When this is empty, Zinc uses the characters shown.

settings.label: Click to move the cursor
settings.description: At a shell prompt, clicking in the command you're typing moves the cursor there. Needs shell integration.

settings.label: Right-click
settings.description: Shift+F10 or the Menu key opens the menu anywhere.

choices.label: Menu
choices.detail: A right-click opens the menu too. It has copy, paste, find, the link or command you clicked, split, and close.

choices.label: Copy or paste
choices.detail: A right-click copies the selection, or pastes when nothing is selected.

settings.label: Open links with
settings.description: Web links and files in the terminal open with this.

choices.label: Ctrl+click
choices.detail: Holding Ctrl underlines the links.

choices.label: Alt+click
choices.detail: Holding Alt underlines the links.

choices.label: A click
choices.detail: Dragging across a link still selects it. A program using the mouse still gets the click.

settings.label: Middle-click pastes
settings.description: Pastes the clipboard unless the program uses the mouse.

settings.label: Focus follows mouse
settings.description: Moving the pointer into a pane focuses it.

settings.label: Copy on select
settings.description: Copies text as soon as you select it. The selection stays.

settings.label: Copy with formatting
settings.description: Copies colors and styles too, for documents and email. Apps that take plain text still get plain text.

settings.label: Paste warning
settings.description: Asks before pasting text with more than one line.

choices.label: Automatic
choices.detail: Zinc asks only when the program would take each line as Enter and run it. A program that marks pastes (bracketed paste) gets no warning.

choices.label: Always
choices.detail: Zinc asks even when the program marks pastes (bracketed paste).

settings.label: Large pastes
settings.description: Asks before pasting more than 5 KB.

settings.label: Programs may copy
settings.description: Copying with OSC 52, as tmux, Neovim, and remote shells do.

settings.label: Programs reading the clipboard
settings.description: Anything running, including a remote host, could read the clipboard.

choices.label: Ask each time
choices.detail: Zinc asks whether to let the program read the clipboard once, for the tab, or not at all.

settings.label: Bell
settings.description: Says what happens when a program rings the bell, for example at a failed tab completion.

choices.label: Tab dot
choices.detail: When you aren't looking at the program's pane, a dot shows on the pane's tab and the taskbar button flashes.

choices.label: Flash the pane
choices.detail: The program's pane flashes, and its tab also gets a dot, as with "Tab dot".

settings.label: Bell sound
settings.description: Plays Windows' default sound too.

settings.label: Visual bell
settings.description: Programs that flash the screen instead of beeping (Git Bash does) ring Zinc's bell, as set in "Bell".

settings.label: Remote control
settings.description: Lets zn, Zinc's command-line tool, open, arrange, and close tabs, type into them, and read them. Any program running as you could use zn.

settings.label: Use zn in other terminals
settings.description: Adds zn to your PATH, so other terminals find zn too. Zinc's own terminals always do. Shells started from now on see the change.

settings.label: Input methods
settings.description: Type Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and more with Windows' input methods (IME). Turn it off if keys behave oddly.

settings.label: Low-latency drawing
settings.description: What you type shows up about one screen refresh sooner. Turn it off if a terminal draws wrong or stops drawing, and open an issue. Applies to terminals opened from now on.

settings.label: Free memory of hidden tabs
settings.description: Background tabs, minimized windows, and the dismissed quick terminal give back their graphics memory and rebuild it when you return. Turn it off if switching tabs flashes. Applies only while "Low-latency drawing" is on.

settings.label: Free memory after
settings.description: This is in seconds unless you add a unit, like `45s` or `2m`.

settings.label: Software rendering
settings.description: Draws with the processor instead of the graphics card, which is slower. Use it for broken graphics drivers, some virtual machines, and remote desktop glitches. Applies to terminals opened from now on.

settings.label: Long command finishes
settings.description: Says what happens when a long command finishes in a pane you weren't looking at.

choices.label: Tab dot
choices.detail: Zinc shows a dot on the pane's tab. The taskbar button also flashes if Zinc is in the background.

choices.label: Notification
choices.detail: Zinc shows a dot on the pane's tab, and a Windows notification if Zinc is in the background.

choices.label: Always notify
choices.detail: Zinc shows a Windows notification whenever you aren't looking at the pane, even while you're using Zinc.

choices.label: None
choices.detail: Zinc shows neither a dot nor a notification.

settings.label: Counts as long after
settings.description: This is in seconds unless you add a unit, like `45s` or `2m`.

settings.label: Sound
settings.description: Plays when a long command finishes out of view. A Windows notification has its own sound.

settings.label: Program notifications
settings.description: Says what happens when a program asks for a notification with OSC 9 or 777, for example when a build script finishes.

choices.label: Tab dot
choices.detail: Zinc shows a dot on the pane's tab. The taskbar button also flashes if Zinc is in the background.

choices.label: Notification
choices.detail: Zinc shows a dot on the pane's tab, and a Windows notification if Zinc is in the background.

choices.label: Always notify
choices.detail: Zinc shows a Windows notification whenever you aren't looking at the pane, even while you're using Zinc.

choices.label: None
choices.detail: Zinc shows neither a dot nor a notification.

settings.label: Finished
settings.description: A command finished, or a program sent a notification.

settings.label: Bell
settings.description: A program rang the bell.

settings.label: Failed
settings.description: A command failed, or a program exited with an error.

settings.label: Hotkey
settings.description: Shows and hides the quick terminal from anywhere, for example `win+grave` or `ctrl+alt+t`.

choices.label: With the pointer
choices.detail: The quick terminal opens on the screen the pointer is on.

choices.label: Main
choices.detail: The quick terminal always opens on the main screen.

settings.label: Size
settings.description: Sets the quick terminal's size along its edge, as a percentage or in pixels (`50%`, `600px`). When empty, the size is 50%, or 70% by 60% at "Center".

settings.label: Animation
settings.description: How long the quick terminal takes to fade in and out. At 0 it appears at once.

settings.label: Check for updates automatically
settings.description: Zinc checks once a day. New versions download in the background, and you choose when to restart. Only a copy installed with Zinc's installer updates itself.

settings.label: Debug log
settings.description: Keeps a record of what Zinc does, to send with a bug report. Turn it on, make the problem happen, then copy the log.

settings.label: SSH hosts
settings.description: Reads hosts from `~/.ssh/config`.

fileOnly.text: Palette colors by number (palette.1 = "#AC4242") are set in config.toml.
Zinc offers the shaders in these folders to choose from. Add and remove folders on the shaders page, in the library's … menu.

profileFields.label: Name
profileFields.description: Menus and tabs show this name.
profileFields.defaultText: The found shell's own name, or else the profile's id

profileFields.label: Command
profileFields.description: The profile's tabs run this shell or other program.
profileFields.defaultText: The found shell's own command, or else PowerShell 7, else Windows PowerShell, else Command Prompt

profileFields.label: Starting folder
profileFields.description: The profile's tabs start in this folder. Write `~` for your home folder, or a path, which can use `%VARIABLES%`.

profileFields.label: Icon
profileFields.description: The profile's tabs show this image file. Without one, they show the program's own icon.

profileFields.label: Hidden
profileFields.description: Keeps the profile out of the menus. Its tabs still reopen.

topLevel.label: Include
topLevel.description: Reads more config files first, by path or pattern. What this file says wins.
topLevel.takes: A path, or a list of paths

topLevel.label: Default profile
topLevel.description: New tabs open with the profile that has this id.
topLevel.defaultText: The first profile in the menu. That's your own first profile, or else the first shell Zinc finds, which is your default WSL distribution when you have one

topLevel.label: Profile order
topLevel.description: The menus list profiles in this order, by id.

topLevel.label: Environment
topLevel.description: Sets environment variables for the programs Zinc starts. An empty value removes that variable.
topLevel.takes: A table of names and values

topLevel.label: Keys
topLevel.description: Binds a key chord or sequence, like `ctrl+shift+t` or `ctrl+a > c`, to the action it runs. A key bound to `none` goes to the program instead.
topLevel.takes: A table of keys and actions
